properties.decision:
ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-15, given after the capture was complete and after he had been shown the collision with `req:sources-are-kept-not-just-parsed`: "for our own reflow2 set of feedback docs; once ingested, please remove (this is my policy just for the reflow2 design because I don't want documents accumulating and have to clean up some day — I want to keep a nice clean repo)".

DISTINCT FROM `rule:design-information-lives-in-the-graph-not-in-documents`, which the guard named: THE RULE SAYS WHAT MAY NOT BE STORED; THIS SAYS WHAT HAPPENS TO A DOCUMENT THAT ALREADY EXISTS ONCE IT HAS BEEN CAPTURED. A prohibition and a lifecycle step. It is also the OBSOLETES source the retirement needs — only an ACCEPTED DECISION withdraws anything from a design, and a DesignRule cannot play that part.

SCOPE, DELIBERATELY NARROW — his own framing, twice: "our own reflow2 set of feedback docs" and "just for the reflow2 design". This governs THIS repository's inbound feedback documents. It is NOT a product position, NOT advice to consumers, and NOT a general answer to where prose belongs. `dec:idea-can-the-graph-be-the-official-record-an-organisation-trusts` holds that larger question and stays open.

THE CONDITION IS 'ONCE INGESTED', WHICH IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART. Removal is licensed by capture having HAPPENED, not by the rule existing. Both documents removed under this decision were captured first, item by item, into TemporalFacts, Decisions and Fragments carrying the reporters' words verbatim — and the un-distilled remainder stays recoverable from git history, so the deletion costs reconstruction detail rather than findings.

⚠️ WHAT THIS KNOWINGLY OVERRIDES, recorded rather than glossed: `req:sources-are-kept-not-just-parsed` is ACCEPTED and says ingest keeps the original corpus documents "so the corpus becomes part of the design rather than an input consumed and discarded". It was left accepted-and-unsatisfied on purpose when `cap:content-store` was discontinued (`dec:the-content-store-is-discontinued`, 2026-08-09), with a `design_artifacts` folder named as the replacement and still unbuilt. HE WAS SHOWN THAT COLLISION AND CHOSE REMOVAL ANYWAY. The requirement's status is his to move and has NOT been moved on his behalf; it stays accepted and unsatisfied, and this decision is the reason a later reader will find them pointing in opposite directions.

WHY HE CHOSE IT, in his words from the same thread: documents "get forgotten and hard to maintain"; a corpus "piling up" is the fear (dev_storyflow's 900+ records now being read slowly); and "documents are external and require grep to see contents… having in the graph is immediately searchable". The backlog file that "kept growing and growing" is the precedent he cites, on the record as `dec:backlog-is-retired`.

MECHANICS: the Artifact nodes are RETIRED ON THE RECORD, not deleted. They keep their names, their checksums — the proof of exactly what was captured — and their Fragments and YIELDED edges, so every finding can still be traced to the document that produced it. OBSOLETES is drawn from this decision to each Artifact (`dec:idea-discontinued-is-a-first-class-state`).
properties.name: reflow2's own feedback documents are deleted once their content is in the graph — a policy for THIS repository, not a claim about how consumers should work
properties.rationale: Recorded as its own accepted Decision rather than merged into the rule after the guard named it: a prohibition on storing and a lifecycle step for what already exists are different acts, and only an accepted Decision can be the source of the OBSOLETES edge that retires the two Artifacts. Accepted on his explicit word given in this session; no status was moved on his behalf, and the requirement it overrides was deliberately left where it stands.
